en: The Philippines is an archipelago composed of exactly 7,641 islands.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, standing at 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River in northern Luzon is the longest river in the country, stretching approximately 505 kilometers.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a surface area of about 911 square kilometers.
Lake Mainit in Mindanao is the deepest lake in the Philippines, reaching a maximum depth of 800 meters.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is highly active, having erupted over 50 times in the past 400 years.
The Philippines is currently divided into 17 distinct administrative regions, including the National Capital Region.
The country is subdivided into exactly 81 provinces, each governed by its own local provincial government.
The Philippines experiences an average annual rainfall of about 2,000 millimeters, with some mountainous areas receiving over 4,000 millimeters.
Approximately 50 percent of the terrestrial wildlife species in the Philippines are endemic, meaning they are found nowhere else.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features a navigable underground river that stretches for 8.2 kilometers.
The Philippine Sea, located east of the archipelago, covers a vast area of about 5 million square kilometers.
